## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5791089552) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5794703669), checked at `caff3e03ef34`.

**Outcome:** the toggle path is fixed and the four helpers now ship, but global mode still does not take effect at this revision. The monitor-base allocator never allocates, the move helper misreads the monitor field, and the bar's global-mode flag can never become true. With the toggle enabled, every config reload also stalls the compositor for about 5 seconds.

| Earlier finding | Status at `caff3e03ef34` |
|---|---|
| Toggle command cannot find the module | **Resolved.** `default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua` is where `omarchy-hyprland-toggle` looks for it |
| Global mode calls missing helpers | **Resolved as stated:** all four are in `bin/`. The described impact (fallback to `monitor.id * 10`) persists through the allocator and move-helper issues below |
| Bar excludes secondary monitors' ranges | **Still present.** The new slot mapping is correct but never activates (see below) |

**Verified:** the `((id - 1) % 10) + 1` bar mapping is correct for multiple-of-10 bases, local mode in the bar and both entry commands is unchanged from base, slot arguments are still validated as 1–10 before interpolation, and the Lua and `hyprctl dispatch` forms used exist in Hyprland 0.56.2.

## `omarchy-monitor-base sync` never allocates a base

[`allocate_bases`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/bin/omarchy-monitor-base#L72-L84) runs `python3 - ... <<'PYEOF'`. The heredoc becomes Python's stdin to supply the program, so the monitor names piped in at [line 130](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/bin/omarchy-monitor-base#L130) never reach `sys.stdin` at line 84.

```text
Isolated run, synthetic hyprctl reporting eDP-1 and HDMI-A-1:
sync as shipped              -> stdout empty, bases file {}
same Python, names on stdin  -> "eDP-1 0", "HDMI-A-1 10"
```

**Impact:** the Lua module always falls back to `monitor.id * 10`, the global switch helper only focuses the raw slot, and `omarchy-ensure-workspaces` exits immediately. This is the impact the earlier "missing helpers" finding described.

**Suggested change:** pass the names as arguments (for example `names = sys.argv[2:]`) or run the program with `-c`, so stdin stays free for the data.

## The move helper looks up a numeric monitor ID as a name

[`omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-move-window`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-move-window#L22-L31) reads `monitor` from `hyprctl activewindow -j`. In Hyprland 0.56.2 that field is the numeric monitor ID (`src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp`, window JSON), while the bases map is keyed by name.

```text
Isolated run, map {"eDP-1":0,"HDMI-A-1":10}, slot 2:
monitor: 1           (Hyprland shape) -> move to workspace "2"
monitor: "HDMI-A-1"  (control)        -> move to workspace "12"
```

**Impact:** even with a populated map, windows move to raw workspace N, which the global rules bind to the base-0 monitor, so the window leaves its monitor.

**Suggested change:** take the monitor name from `hyprctl activeworkspace -j` or from the focused entry of `hyprctl monitors -j`.

## The bar's global-mode flag can never become true

[`Workspaces.qml`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Workspaces.qml#L12-L26) has two independent blockers:

1. `StandardPaths` belongs to the `QtCore` QML module, which the file does not import, so `globalFlagPath` does not resolve to the flag file.
2. Quickshell's `FileView` has no `exists` property (checked in the Quickshell revision Omarchy packages and in upstream sources). `globalModeActive` therefore stays `false`. Even the real `loaded` property would not react to the file appearing, because `watchChanges` is not set.

**Impact:** slot mapping, cross-monitor occupancy and click routing through `omarchy-switch-to-aw` never activate, so workspace 12 still lights no button.

**Suggested change:** follow the existing flag pattern in `shell/Commons/Style.qml` (`windowNoGapsToggle`): build the path with `Quickshell.env("HOME")`, set `watchChanges: true`, and derive the flag from load/failure/change signals, or watch the toggles directory as `Bar.qml` does.

## Config reloads stall for about 5 seconds while the toggle is on

The module calls [`io.popen("omarchy-monitor-base sync")`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua#L53) during config evaluation, and the helper runs `hyprctl monitors -j`.

```text
hyprctl reload / autoreload
  -> Hyprland event loop runs the config synchronously
     -> io.popen: omarchy-monitor-base sync
        -> hyprctl monitors -j   (needs the same event loop to answer)
           -> waits for the hyprctl 5 s receive timeout, returns no monitors
```

Source-derived from Hyprland 0.56.2 (`HyprCtl.cpp` socket handling and `reloadRequest`, `hyprctl/src/main.cpp` timeout), not observed natively. At login the socket does not exist yet, so the call fails quickly instead.

**Impact:** input and rendering pause on every reload with the flag enabled, starting with the reload that `omarchy-hyprland-toggle workspace-global on` issues. That command's own `hyprctl reload` may also time out and report failure after the flag was already copied. The module still receives no bases.

**Suggested change:** avoid IPC from config evaluation. The module already has `hl.get_monitors()` names, so allocate in Lua, or pass those names to the helper as arguments.

## Default workspace keybindings bypass the new commands

[`default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua#L21-L25) still binds SUPER+N and SUPER+SHIFT+N to raw workspace N. Nothing calls `omarchy-move-window-to-aw`, and the only caller of `omarchy-switch-to-aw` is the bar click path above.

**Impact:** in global mode, SUPER+SHIFT+2 on a base-10 monitor sends the window to workspace 2 on the base-0 monitor instead of workspace 12. Switching relies only on the Lua `workspace.active` hook.

**Suggested change:** route these bindings through the global-aware commands (or Lua equivalents) when the flag is on, or document the intended binding setup.

## Hotplug is not picked up until a reload

The module builds its bases, monitor list and workspace rules once per config evaluation ([lines 53–128](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua#L53-L128)) and subscribes only to `workspace.active` (line 234). Hyprland 0.56.2 does not reload the config on hotplug, and `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-watch` reloads only in specific clamshell, mirror and mode cases.

**Impact:** a newly connected monitor is not synced, and a disconnected monitor's stale entry still dispatches its workspace, which Hyprland has moved to another monitor. This conflicts with the stated hotplug support. It becomes visible once the allocator works.

**Suggested change:** handle Hyprland's Lua `monitor.added` / `monitor.removed` events to refresh the map and live monitor set, and dispatch only to connected monitors.

## Global switching moves focus and the pointer off the current monitor

Focusing a workspace owned by another monitor focuses that monitor and warps the pointer to it (Hyprland 0.56.2 `ConfigActions.cpp`, `changeWorkspace`). [The switch helper](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/caff3e03ef34a274464accbce65fa4f8bf6404dc/bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-switch#L44-L51) dispatches every base in ascending order, and the Lua hook dispatches the other monitors without restoring focus.

**Impact:** source-derived, not observed natively. After SUPER+N, keyboard focus and the cursor can end on a different monitor from the one in use. The helper ends on the highest-base monitor.

**Suggested change:** dispatch the originating monitor last, or refocus it after syncing.

**Test note:** `test/cli` requires `# omarchy:summary=` in the header of every executable `bin/omarchy-*`. The six scripts this PR adds lack it, and the repository's metadata loop, run in isolation, reports them missing at this head and none at base. Adding summary lines (and `# omarchy:hidden=true` for internal helpers) fixes it.

**Cleanup:** `config/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua` is still in the tree. Nothing loads it, but it ships to users' config directories as a stale duplicate.

---

**Test scope:** pinned-source inspection of `caff3e03ef34` with Hyprland 0.56.2, Quickshell and Qt QML source. Isolated command runs with a synthetic `hyprctl` stub covered the allocator, the move helper's monitor lookup and the CLI metadata check. No native Hyprland, bar rendering, multi-monitor, hotplug or reload-timing test was run. The reload stall, focus movement and hotplug results are source-derived.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, with independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this revision and targeted cross-checks of claims first raised by only one reviewer. Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
